message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills and modern scares you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** (1980) | A psychological masterpiece with haunting imagery and an unforgettable performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** (2018) | A slow‑burn family drama that turns into a terrifying descent into grief and supernatural dread. |
| 3 | **Get Out** (2017) | A smart social thriller that blends horror with sharp satire—perfect if you want something thought‑provoking. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Suspenseful, tense, and relies on sound design to keep you on edge. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** (2019) | A daylight horror that subverts expectations with its unsettling folk‑ritual atmosphere. |
| 6 | **It Follows** (2014) | A fresh take on the “invisible stalker” trope with a creepy soundtrack and practical effects. |
| 7 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | A well‑crafted paranormal investigation that delivers genuine scares without over‑reliance on jump‑scares. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** (2014) | An emotional story about grief that becomes a psychological nightmare. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** (1977) | For fans of surreal, atmospheric horror—its color palette and score are iconic. |
|10 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (2012) | A meta‑commentary on horror tropes that still delivers plenty of gore and laughs. |

Feel free to pick one or two depending on how intense you want your Friday night to be!
